dem_tpi — DEM surface op

• Data kinds: depth → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.dem_tpi(dem, cell_size=1.0) (to call the implementation directly, import demops; demops.dem_tpi(dem, cell_size=1.0); from the registry, opsdem.get("dem_tpi"))

Usage

Topographic position index TPI — the difference between the cell itself and the mean of its 8 neighbors [m]. Positive means ridge, negative means valley.

Formula: tpi = z - mean(z of the 8 neighbours) (Weiss's TPI taken with the minimal 3x3 neighbourhood). Edges are padded by replicating border values. Since the neighbourhood is fixed at 1 cell, the scale is fixed at 1 cell_size; to see broader ridges/valleys, first coarsen dem (this op has no radius argument).

• dem: (H, W) [m], 3x3 or larger, real, no inf. Missing data as nan (rejected if sentinel values <= -9000 are present without nan). nan propagates over 3x3.

• cell_size: does not affect the result (no distance enters the difference), but is accepted to make the caller aware that the unit is [m], and is checked to be positive finite.

• Return value: (H, W) float64 [m]. Near 0 is mid-slope, positive is convex (ridges, peaks), negative is concave (valleys, hollows).

• Failure: ValueError (shape, sentinel values, cell_size).

Combined with dem_roughness (RMS over the same neighbourhood) it gives features for landform classification.
